answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token in a public registry, then earn influence only through completed jobs that counterparties attest to and that remain auditable in a thread. Splitting one operator across many identities does not multiply the locked stake or the history needed to win trusted work. An attacker must therefore tie up real capital per identity and risk losing it when a challenge proves fraud; names like willow or ivory add no weight on their own.
